systems.name: Linear Harmony Outline System
systems.summary: The central system of this book is a graph whose members are the three melodic outlines (plus their fragment variants) that structure ii–V–I improvisation. The outlines are not interchangeable shapes but distinct motion-types — stepwise descent, ascending arpeggio, descending arpeggio — each operating over the same two-chord progression. Movement between outlines is governed by voice-leading rules that prioritize the seventh-to-third resolution chain as the connective tissue crossing barlines. Modification rules govern how any outline member may be embellished or reduced without losing harmonic clarity. The system generalizes to any root-motion-by-fifths progression including minor ii–V, modal contexts, and turnarounds.

members.name: Outline No. 1 — Stepwise Descent
members.summary: Begins on the third of the ii chord, descends stepwise through the V7, and resolves to the third of the I chord.

members.name: Outline No. 2 — Ascending Arpeggio
members.summary: Arpeggiation of the ii chord (1–3–5–7); seventh resolves to the third of V7 on the V7 chord itself.

members.name: Outline No. 3 — Descending Arpeggio
members.summary: Descends the ii chord (5–3–1), adds the seventh below as a pointer tone resolving to the third of V7.

members.name: Outline Fragment
members.summary: Partial version with omissions; harmonic coherence maintained provided target tones are placed and resolved.

members.name: Guide-Tone Pair (Third and Seventh)
members.summary: The third supplies harmonic specificity; the seventh is the restless pointer that drives resolution downward.

traversal_rules.name: Seventh-to-Third Resolution
traversal_rules.summary: The seventh of each chord resolves downward to the third of the following chord.

references.quote_excerpt: the 7th of chords in these progressions resolve downward to the third of the following chord. The seventh is the pointer.

traversal_rules.name: Third-Before-Seventh Placement
traversal_rules.summary: Within any melodic line, the third appears earlier than the seventh.

references.quote_excerpt: Thirds are more consonant and usually occur earlier in a melody line before the more dissonant sevenths.

traversal_rules.name: Root Omission for Counterpoint
traversal_rules.summary: The root is omitted from melodic lines because the bass covers it.

references.quote_excerpt: Eliminating the root leaves eleven other notes to choose from; all of which are used by jazz artists.

traversal_rules.name: Punch Line Rule
traversal_rules.summary: In Outline No. 2, the target note is withheld until the V7 chord arrives.

references.quote_excerpt: This tone is usually saved for the V7 chord. It is the punch line, the denouement of the story, that is not given away by using it ahead of time as a passing tone.

traversal_rules.name: Target-Tone Rhythmic Placement on Strong Beats
traversal_rules.summary: Thirds and sevenths land on metrically significant beats so chromatic non-chord tones are heard as embellishment.

references.quote_excerpt: Target notes occur in rhythmically significant spots, non-harmonic chromatic notes resolve when and where we expect them.

traversal_rules.name: Multi-Outline Sequential Combination
traversal_rules.summary: Outlines may be combined sequentially; most common combination joins Outline No. 2 with Outline No. 1.

references.quote_excerpt: Parker begins with outline no.2 and ends with outline no.1.

traversal_rules.name: Universal Root-Motion-by-Fifths Applicability
traversal_rules.summary: Any of the three outlines may be applied to any progression whose root motion descends by fifths.

references.quote_excerpt: Anytime the root movement is down in fifths any of theses outlines will work, regardless of the quality of the chord.

modification_rules.name: C.E.S.H. — Chromatic Elaboration of Static Harmony
modification_rules.summary: A descending chromatic line is superimposed over the static ii–V progression.

references.quote_excerpt: The most common example in a ii - V progression is the descending movement from the root of the ii chord to the third of the V7 chord, In the key of C (D minor - G7), the movement of D-C#-C-B.

modification_rules.name: Parallel Minor Borrowing on Dominant
modification_rules.summary: Flat-9, sharp-9, and flat-13 borrowed from the parallel minor over dominant chords.

references.quote_excerpt: Over G7, the dominant of C major, jazz musicians often use A-flat (flat 9) , B-flat (sharp 9) and E-flat (flat 13) from the parallel key of C minor.

modification_rules.name: Octave Displacement
modification_rules.summary: A melodic step replaced by its compound equivalent — third-to-second becomes ascending seventh to the ninth.

references.quote_excerpt: A simple descending scale step (3-2) becomes dramatic when a descending second is replaced with a leap of a seventh.

modification_rules.name: Chromatic Directional Tendency Rule
modification_rules.summary: Flatted notes continue downward; sharped notes continue upward.

references.quote_excerpt: Chromatically altered tones tend to continue in the direction in which they have been altered.

modification_rules.name: Diatonic UNT / Chromatic LNT Convention
modification_rules.summary: Upper neighbor tones diatonic; lower neighbor tones chromatic.

references.quote_excerpt: The common practice (from Mozart to Charlie Parker) is to use the diatonic (from the key) upper neighbor tone (UNT) and the chromatic lower neighbor tone (LNT).

modification_rules.name: Outline Fragmentation
modification_rules.summary: Non-target chord tones may be omitted provided target tones are placed and resolved.

references.quote_excerpt: Fragments of outlines have been previously shown where harmonic clarity was still present with some of the elements missing.

modification_rules.name: Encircling Target-Tone Surrounding
modification_rules.summary: Target note approached from both above (diatonic UNT) and below (chromatic LNT) in succession.

references.quote_excerpt: He chooses to encircle the target note, creating a slight tension and ambiguity.

modification_rules.name: Compound Melody via Register Split
modification_rules.summary: Single line implies two voices via third-to-flat-nine leap on the dominant.

references.quote_excerpt: The leap from the third to the flat nine on the dominant is one of its attractive elements; giving it characteristics of a compound melody.

modification_rules.name: Bebop Outline Superimposition over Modal Harmony
modification_rules.summary: Bebop outlines layered over modal harmony via leading-tone approach.

references.quote_excerpt: Some jazz improvisers bring some of the be-bop vocabulary with them when playing on modal pieces.
